brief: Eight geometric constructions of the selected Overlap C. Keep the same teal/blue palette and vary circle, square and polygon geometry.

concepts.name: Radial
concepts.idea: Concentric circles with clean radial cuts.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Create one geometric redesign of the attached Codealong Overlap C logo. The reference supplies ONLY the idea (a right-opening C built from a turquoise upper component and cobalt lower component with a darker shared area at left). Completely redraw the contours using the specific geometric construction below. Do not copy the source's organic bean-shaped overlap or wobbly varying-width silhouette. This should look like precise 2D vector geometry drawn with shape tools.
Palette: exactly three uniform solid color areas: upper turquoise #43CEC9, lower cobalt #315CF6, overlap dark blue #145B91. Opaque flat fills. Absolutely no gradients, texture, shading, highlights, lighting, shadows, bevels, perspective, ribbon folds, 3D, material simulation, outline strokes, decorative details or additional symbols. Flat mathematical geometry is essential. No text or labels. One mark only, centered on a pure white square canvas, occupying 68% of canvas height with even whitespace. No tile or mockup. Horizontal symmetry in the overall silhouette unless specifically stated. Keep an obvious right-facing C opening and generous negative space. The overlap is an explicit flat third-color region, not a lighting effect.

Construction: Build a C from a perfect circular annulus with outer radius 100 and inner radius 58. Remove a 90-degree wedge pointing right. Both terminals are straight radial cuts at plus/minus 45 degrees. The remaining 270-degree ring has exactly constant width. Upper half turquoise and lower half cobalt, overlapping in a dark concentric annular sector centered at the far left, spanning 50 degrees. That overlap is bounded by two straight radial lines; it is not a lens or curved blob. No rounded caps anywhere.

Construction: Build a perfect circular C as a constant-width circular arc with exact semicircular caps at the two terminals. The arc centerline sweeps 250 degrees and leaves a wide right opening. Uniform band thickness is 40 percent of the outer radius. Both terminal caps are precisely the same diameter as the band thickness. Upper arc turquoise, lower arc cobalt, overlapping in one short dark annular sector centered at nine o'clock. Both overlap boundaries are straight radial cuts. No organic lens, no swelling or tapering. Circular counter concentric with outer contour.

Construction: Construct an upright square C with horizontal top and bottom arms and a vertical left spine. Outer left corners are exact quarter circles with radius 40; inner left corners exact quarter circles radius 12. Straight band thickness 28 everywhere. Top and bottom arms end on the same right vertical line with sharp square flat terminals. Turquoise upper component and cobalt lower component meet in one small dark rectangular overlap at the center of the vertical left spine. All horizontal and vertical edges parallel to the canvas. Large square negative space, softly rounded only at its two left corners. No capsule tips, no organic lens.

They share a simple dark square midway on the left spine. Continuous coherent C silhouette, rectangular counter fully open to the right. Equal bar thickness 28 relative to outer width 100; outer height 112. No diagonal lines, no curves, no rounded corners, no isometric perspective.

Construction: Build a C from exactly two geometric half-annuli. The top half is turquoise, the bottom half cobalt. Both use the exact same outer and inner radii, thickness 32 percent of the diameter, and entirely circular outlines. Horizontally offset the two semicircular bands by only 8 percent of their diameter so they overlap at left while leaving a broad right-facing opening. Use simple straight-cut ends at the opening. The common left region is dark blue; show one simple clean polygon-or-arc bounded shared region. Their slight offset is deliberate and measured, never organic or swollen. The outer silhouette may have one tiny step at left from the offset, but remain a coherent C.
